interest: Shows U.S. dealings with Hirohito shifting from ceremonial greetings in 1940–41 to wartime debate over the Imperial House.
overview: List of Papers for 894.001 H 61 on Emperor Hirohito, 1940–1944: anniversary and birthday greetings, the 'Hot Mikado' cartoon, and wartime debate on the Imperial House.

people.role: State Department official, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Sotomatsu Kato
people.role: First Secretary of the Japanese Embassy in Washington

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew advises the State Department that February 11, 1940, is the appropriate date for President Roosevelt to congratulate Emperor Hirohito on the 2600th anniversary of the accession of Emperor Jimmu.
subfiles.summary: Grew's Telegram No. 44 reports the Foreign Office suggested February 11, 1940, for congratulations on the 2600th anniversary of Emperor Jimmu's accession.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew on 2600th Anniversary of Accession of Emperor Jimmu

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo that President Roosevelt's congratulatory message to the Emperor will be sent on February 11, 1940.
subfiles.from: Department of State (FE, Joseph W. Ballantine)
subfiles.summary: State Department Telegram No. 53 tells the Tokyo embassy Roosevelt will send the Emperor a message on February 11.
subfiles.title: Telegram from State Department on Presidential Message for Imperial Anniversary

subfiles.about: A memorandum of conversation details Japanese Embassy objections to an American newspaper cartoon referring to the Emperor as the 'Hot Mikado'.
subfiles.from: Sotomatsu Kato and Joseph W. Ballantine
subfiles.summary: A memorandum of conversation between Mr. Kato, First Secretary of the Japanese Embassy, and State Department official Ballantine (Dillantine) records Japanese objections to an American newspaper cartoon labeled the 'Hot Mikado'. The Japanese Embassy considered the cartoon objectionable and disrespectful to Emperor Hirohito, prompting diplomatic representations to the U.S. government.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Objectionable 'Hot Mikado' Cartoon

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt extends official ceremonial birthday greetings to Emperor Hirohito on April 29, 1940.
subfiles.summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt transmits official ceremonial greetings to Emperor Hirohito on the occasion of his birthday on April 29, 1940. The exchange records the continuing observation of formal diplomatic protocol between the heads of state of the United States and Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram of Presidential Birthday Greetings to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Ambassador Claude Bowers reports on the celebration of the 2600th Japanese imperial anniversary in Chile and the Emperor's appreciation for presidential greetings.
subfiles.summary: U.S. Ambassador to Chile Claude G. Bowers submits Despatch No. 488 reporting on celebrations held in Chile commemorating the 2600th anniversary of the Japanese Empire. The docket entry also records that the Emperor expressed appreciation to President Roosevelt for his birthday greetings.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Bowers on Japanese Anniversary Celebrations in Chile

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits the full texts of President Roosevelt's 1940 messages to Emperor Hirohito regarding his birthday and the imperial accession anniversary.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew sends Telegram No. 954 from Tokyo quoting the official texts of previous presidential messages to Emperor Hirohito. These include the April 29, 1940 birthday greetings and the February 11, 1940 message congratulating the Emperor on the 2600th anniversary of the accession of Emperor Jimmu.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew Quoting Texts of Presidential Messages

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note records a suggested revision to Ambassador Grew's scheduled address at the celebration of the founding of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on a suggested revision of Grew's address for the November 11 imperial anniversary celebration.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Address by Ambassador Grew for Imperial Celebration

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt extends birthday congratulations to Emperor Hirohito in April 1941, and the Emperor expresses his appreciation.
subfiles.from: President Franklin D. Roosevelt / Emperor Hirohito
subfiles.summary: On April 29, 1941, President Franklin D. Roosevelt sends telegraphic birthday congratulations to Emperor Hirohito. The Emperor responds by expressing his appreciation to the President for his good wishes, marking the final peacetime exchange of birthday greetings between the two heads of state before the outbreak of the Pacific War.
subfiles.title: Telegram on Birthday Congratulations and Emperor's Appreciation
subfiles.to: Emperor Hirohito / President Franklin D. Roosevelt

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note records an inquiry from Reuters to New York City Mayor La Guardia regarding post-war maintenance of the Japanese Imperial House.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on a Reuters request asking Mayor Fiorello H. La Guardia whether Japan's Imperial House should be kept after victory.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Mayor La Guardia and Post-War Status of Imperial House

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum discusses an article in The New Leader arguing against preserving the imperial institution in post-war Japan.
subfiles.summary: State Department official Hooker (AB/H) submits a memorandum addressing a published article in The New Leader entitled 'The Hirohito Myth'. The article critiques the Emperor's role and advocates dismantling or overturning the institution of the Emperor in post-war Japan, illustrating contemporary wartime debates over United States policy toward Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Hooker on New Leader Article 'The Hirohito Myth'
